title: The Art of Everyday Dressing
body: A thoughtful wardrobe does not need a new answer every morning. Begin with a piece you already love, then let its shape guide the rest: the Elise Dress beneath a soft cardigan, or the Margot Blouse paired with familiar trousers. Repeating a combination is not a lack of imagination; it is how personal style gathers meaning. Notice what feels easy to move in, what you reach for again, and which small changes make an old favourite feel fresh. Everyday dressing becomes an art of attention, rather than accumulation.
excerpt: Build a personal style through thoughtful combinations, repeat wear and the pieces that feel most like you.

title: A Soft Autumn
body: As the season turns, layering can feel less like preparation and more like a quiet pleasure. Let a fine knit sit beneath a jacket, or bring the Fleur Cardigan over a familiar dress. A skirt and blouse gain a softer mood with a warm layer close at hand. Keep the shapes easy, allowing each piece room to be seen and worn comfortably. Autumn dressing need not begin with a complete change of wardrobe. Often, one well-loved layer is enough to make familiar pieces feel newly in season.
excerpt: Welcome the changing season with gentle layers and familiar pieces made new by the way you wear them.

title: Behind the Atelier
body: Imagine an atelier table where fabric rests beside a page of loose sketches. A line is drawn, reconsidered, and softened; a silhouette takes shape not as a rule, but as a feeling. Perhaps the thought begins with a sleeve, a gathered waist or the graceful fall of a skirt. In this imagined creative process, vintage references meet the ease of everyday dressing. The aim is not perfection on paper, but a sense of balance: something feminine, quietly expressive and easy to picture in motion.
excerpt: An imagined creative process moves from fabric and sketches to silhouettes with feeling and ease.

title: Romantic Silhouettes, Everyday Ease
body: A romantic silhouette feels most at home when balanced by something simple. Pair the soft line of the Madeleine Dress with an unfussy knit, or let the Margot Blouse meet the grounded shape of the Colette Trousers. The contrast keeps a look from feeling too carefully composed: a flowing hem beside a clean jacket, a delicate neckline with familiar separates. Choose one detail to lead, then let the rest of the outfit settle around it. Romance, worn this way, belongs to the everyday rather than a special occasion.
excerpt: Balance feminine shapes with straightforward separates for a look that feels romantic, relaxed and wearable.

title: Fabric Notes
body: Texture can set the mood before a single colour does. Cotton brings a familiar, easy presence to a blouse; linen suggests a relaxed line, especially alongside pieces with a softer drape. Fine knits add quiet depth, whether worn close to the body or layered over a simple top. Think of these fabrics as styling cues, not instructions: mix a smooth surface with a more tactile one, or keep the textures gentle and tonal. The pleasure is in noticing how each material changes the way a silhouette feels.
excerpt: Let the feel of cotton, linen and fine knits inspire thoughtful texture and gentle contrast.

title: The Frunză Woman
body: The Frunză woman is less a fixed image than a way of dressing: attentive, individual and quietly at ease. She may choose the Jeanne Skirt with a simple knit, or the Simone Jacket over pieces she already knows by heart. Vintage references appeal to her, but she wears them in her own rhythm, with no need to make an entrance. Her style leaves room for softness and practicality, for repetition and small surprises. What makes it hers is not a perfect formula, but the care she brings to choosing.
excerpt: A fictional portrait of quiet individuality, shaped by familiar favourites and a personal sense of ease.
